resources.string: Pay without internet
Pay without internet
Pay any UPI ID with *99#. Needs only phone signal.
Pay by UPI when there\'s no internet
No internet, but a bar of phone signal? You can still pay by UPI. *99# is your bank\'s own service: it runs on plain phone signal and asks for everything itself.
Pay with *99#
This phone has no Phone app, so it can\'t use *99#.
You have internet right now, so your usual UPI app will be quicker. This way is for when you don\'t.
No phone signal right now. *99# needs ordinary signal — try again when you have a bar.
This phone\'s SIM looks like Jio, and *99# doesn\'t work on Jio. If your bank has the number of another SIM in this phone, choose that SIM when the Phone app opens.
How to pay
Tap Pay with *99#. The Phone app opens with *99*1*3# typed in. Press call — on the SIM your bank has.
Type the UPI ID you\'re paying, like name@bank. A shop\'s QR sticker usually has it printed under the code.
Your bank shows the name on that UPI ID. If it\'s who you mean to pay, type the amount.
When it asks for a remark, send 1 to skip it.
Type your UPI PIN and send. The PIN shows as you type, so keep the screen to yourself.
Your bank shows whether it went through, and sends you an SMS.

Good to know
Up to ₹5,000 at a time. Your bank may allow less in a day.
Works on Airtel, Vi, BSNL and MTNL. Not on Jio.
Call from the SIM whose number your bank has.
Paying a bill shown on a card machine or a website this way may fail, or the shop may not see which bill you paid. A shop\'s printed UPI ID works best.
Hopline never sees your UPI PIN. You type it into your phone company\'s own box.
Never used *99#? Set it up once. You\'ll need your debit card, and no internet.
Set up *99#
If it doesn\'t work
“Connection problem or invalid MMI code” — that SIM can\'t reach *99#. It may be Jio, or have no signal. Try your other SIM.
It asked for your language or your bank — *99# isn\'t set up on that number yet. Set it up, then pay again.
It showed a menu instead of asking for the UPI ID — choose Send Money, then UPI ID.
It said the UPI ID is wrong — check every letter, and the part after the @. Some networks cut a UPI ID short at the @; if it keeps failing, try your other SIM.
It said declined or failed — your bank may have reached its limit for the day, or the shop\'s UPI ID can\'t be paid this way.
Not sure if the money left? Don\'t pay twice. Open *99#, choose Transactions, and look.
